protected_invariants: the provider enum stays CLOSED: exactly one provider was admitted by this mission ('aws-s3', for the reason recorded in the source comment), the loader still refuses every value outside the admitted set, and a test still asserts that an unrecognised provider string is refused -- widening the enum must never degrade into accepting arbitrary provider values

the region is validated against the provider it was named with rather than against a flat union, because the region vocabularies of the two admitted providers do not overlap and a pair drawn from two providers names a target that cannot resolve; a test pins both the refusal of the cross pair and the acceptance of the in-provider pair

the create-only invariant is unchanged and is never emulated: the S3-compatible transport still sends If-None-Match: '*' on PutObject, a HEAD-then-PUT emulation is never used, and only 412 and 409 are classified as a benign precondition collision

the no-delete invariant is unchanged: the transport still admits exactly five verbs (putObjectCreateOnly, getObject, headObject, listObjects, describe), still refuses all fourteen forbidden verbs including every delete and bucket-administration verb, DELETE_CAPABILITY_EXPOSED=NO, and no delete capability is required from the selected provider

credential handling is unchanged and remains explicit: no default location, no profile, no environment variable, no instance metadata and no provider chain is added to any loader by this mission, and the target-identity schema remains a closed non-secret allowlist that refuses a credential pasted into a field or used as a JSON key

no secret value is created, requested, read, printed, logged, copied or persisted by this mission, CREDENTIAL_CREATED=NO and CREDENTIAL_VALUE_INSPECTED=NO, and no credential value appears in the repository, the diff, a test fixture or an evidence file

the capability claim is not overstated in either direction: the selected provider's atomic create-only capability is recorded as DOCUMENTED_SUPPORTED and NOT live-proven, every artifact that reports it says so, and no artifact claims that a live capability probe was performed, because no provider credential exists on this host and the probe is BLOCKED_OWNER_PROVISIONING

the two offline CLIs (scripts/ops/stage_d_backup_snapshot.js and scripts/ops/stage_d_restore_verify.js) remain byte-unchanged and netless; the refused inline-secret flag lists and the ACCEPTED_FLAGS allowlist in the two live CLIs are likewise unchanged, because the guarantee that a credential cannot be passed on a command line rests on an allowlist rather than on a denylist of known-bad spellings and is therefore provider-independent

the bucket-name pattern is left byte-unchanged because it is already a strict subset of both admitted providers' rules; only its stated provenance is corrected, and it is deliberately the intersection rather than the union so that a name one admitted provider accepts and another refuses is caught here as a provisioning mistake

no provider is contacted and no infrastructure is created: no object-storage request of any kind is issued to any provider, NO_PROVIDER_BUCKET_CREATED=YES, NO_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_CREATED=YES, no paid subscription is created, and no Cloudflare R2 checkout or Backblaze B2 work is resumed

no production state is mutated: no production backup, production restore, production authority mutation, live fetch, DB write, raw write, training, prediction, backtest, model activation or migration apply is executed, and no real Stage D snapshot is written anywhere
